subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which minimum guardrails must stay core versus plugin or ClawHub?
rationale: The request spans storage model, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent product shape.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance/API seam, while workflow-specific audit/review classes live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own the temp artifact registry, classes, and janitor semantics for first-class OpenClaw-created temp artifacts, accepting broader storage and cleanup responsibility.

options.title: Plugin/ClawHub provenance only
options.body: The broad provenance model would stay outside core, with this issue narrowed to concrete runtime-critical temp-path bug reports and missing extension APIs.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance/API seam, while workflow-specific audit/review classes live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history on temp-boundary hardening, security docs, and the related product-scope ClawHub decision.
